question: At identical immutable 32x32 BGRX bytes, does a CPython C-extension exact target counter reduce predicate cost versus the existing Python byte loop without any count or >=512 classification change?
primary_intervention: predicate implementation only: Python byte loop versus native CPython extension; both receive the exact same bytes objects and return exact counts
schedule: 16 paired blocks; even pair Python->native, odd pair native->Python; identical deterministic rotated corpus order within pair; one measured block only
measurement: perf_counter_ns wall plus thread_time_ns current-thread CPU; process pinned to the minimum CPU in its allowed affinity set before warmup and measurement; GC disabled only during warmup/measured blocks
correctness_gate: all 512 expected counts, Python counts, native counts and >=512 classifications exactly equal; wrong-length and wrong-type native inputs reject

decision.PASS_COST_SCOPED: semantic gate passes and both median paired candidate/baseline wall and thread-CPU ratios <= 1/3
decision.HOLD_COST: semantic gate passes but either cost ratio exceeds 1/3

stopping: No retry, no extra pair, no gate change after measured output. A negative result completes this rung.
limits: Offline CPython microbenchmark only. No X server acquisition, input authority, rendering, GUI reliability, hard-real-time, shared-runtime or end-to-end speed claim. CPU frequency is not pinned; compiler/CPython ABI/cache effects are part of or limit the implementation comparison.
